name: Stella
tagline: iOS app that turns goals into AI-generated affirmations, scripting prompts and daily reminders.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The generative part is close to free: an LLM will happily produce affirmations, scripting prompts and reframes for any goal you type, and storing them in a local database is a first-hour task. The hard part is that this category is a delivery mechanism, not a content problem. The value shows up as a phone in your hand at 7am, a lock screen widget, a notification you actually tap, and none of that comes free in a self-hosted web app. You can get most of the way with an installable PWA and web push, but iOS push on PWAs is fussy and widgets are off the table entirely. Build it if the ritual matters more than the packaging; keep the app if you need it to feel like a product rather than a localhost tab.
coreLoopDIY: You enter an intention, an LLM generates a set of affirmations and journaling prompts around it, and the app stores them locally and pushes you a scheduled one each day.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
A always-on host or cheap VPS if you want reliable scheduled notifications
VAPID keys for web push, and an iOS device willing to install the PWA to home screen
whatYouLose: Native iOS notifications, widgets and lock screen presence that actually get seen
Any writing or voice work that someone edited by hand rather than generating on the fly
Sync and backup across devices without you owning the server
The polish that makes a daily practice feel like a practice instead of a form
Whatever audio, streak visuals or guided content the paid app ships
moatNotes: In wellness apps the moat is almost entirely feel: typography, timing, and whether the copy sounds like a person. That is hard to spec and easy to underestimate.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays for affirmation text, they pay for the thing showing up without being maintained. A five dollar a month app that nudges you daily beats a superior self-hosted version you forget to redeploy, and manifestation apps in particular sell a mood: sound, animation, phrasing that does not read like a chatbot. If you are the kind of person who keeps a local project alive, build it. If you are the kind of person who downloads a manifestation app, the subscription is doing real work.
notes: The generator is trivial; the habit loop is the product.
prompt:
Build a personal manifestation and affirmation app called Beacon. Single project, no accounts, single user: me.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/beacon.db, migrations in a plain SQL file run at boot
- LLM calls through the Anthropic Messages API, key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local
- Installable PWA: manifest, service worker, web push using VAPID keys from .env.local
- node-cron inside a small worker script for scheduled pushes

Data model: intentions (title, why it matters, target date, tone preference), generated items (affirmation | scripting prompt | reframe, text, intention_id, created_at), journal entries (item_id nullable, body, mood 1-5, created_at), settings (delivery times, timezone).

Flows:
1. Add an intention in free text. Generate 12 affirmations, 5 scripting prompts and 3 reframes for it in one LLM call, strictly typed JSON out, validated with zod, retried once on parse failure.
2. Today screen: one item of the day, big type, dark background, swipe or button to journal against it. Show a streak count.
3. Library: browse and edit intentions, regenerate items, favourite or delete individual lines.
4. Journal: reverse chronological entries with mood, filterable by intention.
5. Scheduler: at each configured delivery time, pick an unseen or favourited item and send a web push linking to Today.

In scope: local-only storage, manual export to JSON, seed script with one example intention, a /health route.
Out of scope: auth, multi-user, payments, analytics, telemetry, audio, cloud sync, any App Store packaging.

Deliver a README that states exactly how to generate VAPID keys, how to install the PWA on iOS from Safari's share sheet, and the honest caveat that iOS web push only fires for home-screen installs and is not as reliable as a native app.
